article.headline: Quanta Services Wires The Data Center Boom As Profit Nearly Doubles
article.deck: Quanta is building a seven-week cup with a 724.90 buy point and closed 3.3% below it.
body: Quanta Services builds and maintains the physical plant behind the power grid. Its crews design, construct, upgrade and repair electric transmission and distribution lines and substations, install smart grid equipment, and do similar work for gas utilities, power generators, pipelines, communications networks and the large load centers that data centers represent. It is a contractor, not a utility, and it gets paid as the grid gets bigger.

The grid is getting bigger. In the June quarter, Quanta's earnings rose 94.7% to $2.96 a share and revenue climbed 41.1% to $9.56 billion. The step-up was sharp: revenue had been $7.63 billion, $7.84 billion and $7.87 billion in the three quarters before, then jumped to $9.56 billion. Earnings over the same stretch went $2.24, $2.08, $1.45 and then $2.96. The next report is due Oct. 29.

The market is paying for that. Quanta carries a $105.4 billion market value and trades at 35.5 times forward earnings, against 80.3 times trailing earnings. Shares are up 66.1% this year and 63.9% over 12 months. Quanta is one of the leaders of the desk's AI infrastructure group and ranks 86 of 99 on the desk's list.

The chart shows a stock repairing a deeper correction. Quanta hit 788.75 on May 6 and fell to 554.12 by July 29. Since then it has built a seven-week cup, 18.1% deep from its Aug. 17 high to its Sept. 1 low, with a 724.90 buy point and a buy range up to 761.14. The stock remains 11.1% below that May high.

On Wednesday Quanta fell 18.49, or 2.6%, to 701.07 on volume 0.97 times the 50-day average. The close is 3.3% below the buy point. The stock trades 8.1% above its 50-day line at 648.43, with the 21-day line at 657.87. The relative strength line is 15.7% below its high, a lag the stock would need to close before a clean breakout.

The headlines frame Quanta as a data center play. One noted that Big Tech will spend $735 billion on data centers and called Quanta the electrical contractor that collects the checks. Another weighed Quanta against MasTec and asked whether better cash flow is worth a 73% earnings premium. Jim Cramer called it a no-brainer data center buy.
For an engineering and construction firm, revenue growth of 41.1% in a quarter is the mark of a company riding the AI power build-out.
article.watch: A move through 724.90 on heavy volume, and the Oct. 29 earnings report.

article.headline: AbbVie Rises 1.8% As FDA Grants Two Breakthrough Therapy Designations
article.deck: AbbVie broke out of a 10-week flat base past a 267.57 buy point on above-average volume and is 1.4% into a buy range that runs to 280.95.
body: AbbVie rose 4.67, or 1.8%, to 271.36, clearing a 10-week flat base with a 267.57 buy point. The base ran 9.8% deep from its July 29 high to its Aug. 6 low. Volume came in at 5,475,359 shares, 1.17 times the 50-day average, enough to qualify but not a heavy-volume breakout. The close is 1.4% above the buy point and inside the buy range, which runs to 280.95.

The stock sits 1.3% below its 52-week high of 274.94. It trades 5.0% above its 50-day line at 258.33, with the 21-day line at 263.27. The relative strength line is 3.4% below its high and lagged the price breakout, and the stock ranks 65 of 99 on the desk's list, middling for a breakout. Shares are up 18.8% this year.

June-quarter earnings jumped 290.4% to $2.03 a share on revenue up 10.2% to $16.99 billion. The earnings record is uneven: 10 cents, $1.02 and 39 cents in the three quarters before. The next report is due Oct. 30. AbbVie trades at 16.7 times forward earnings with a $479.5 billion market value.

AbbVie said Wednesday that its drug telisotuzumab adizutecan, or Temab-A, received two Breakthrough Therapy designations from the FDA, for colorectal cancer and non-small cell lung cancer. A separate report said an AbbVie treatment cut the risk of progression or death in frontline DLBCL by 51%.
With the report three weeks out, the breakout has a short runway before the numbers decide it.

The company provides a cloud-based security solution to secure a range of combination of platforms, including public and private cloud, on-premises, software-as-a-service applications, and Internet of things (IoT) devices; and application security products comprising web application firewall, bot management, distributed denial of service mitigation, API security, SSL/TLS encryption, client-side security, and security center products. It also offers application performance solutions

article.headline: Cloudflare Falls 3.4% In Light Trade As Basin Data Platform Expands
article.deck: Cloudflare is 3.2% past the 332.32 buy point of a five-week cup, inside a buy range that runs to 348.94.
body: Cloudflare fell 12.04, or 3.4%, to 342.97 on volume of 2,322,751 shares, 0.66 times the 50-day average. The stock broke out of a five-week cup with a 332.32 buy point on Sept. 17, 14 sessions ago, on volume 0.88 times average, a below-average breakout. The cup ran 18.9% deep from its Aug. 13 high to its Sept. 2 low. The close is 3.2% above the buy point and inside the buy range, which runs to 348.94.

The stock is 7.4% below its 52-week high of 370.35. It closed just above the 21-day line at 338.65 and 9.6% above the 50-day line at 313.04. The relative strength line is 5.6% below its high, and the stock ranks 90 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 20.6% in a month and 74.0% this year.

Revenue rose 35.9% to $696.1 million in the June quarter, after $562.0 million, $614.5 million and $639.8 million in the three quarters before. Losses widened through the same stretch: breakeven, then losses of 3 cents, 7 cents and 48 cents a share. The forward P/E is 204.6 on a $122.1 billion market value. The next report is due Oct. 29.
Headlines covered the expansion of Cloudflare's data platform and asked whether Basin is the next growth driver. Another said brokers suggest investing in the stock.
A close below the 21-day line would point the stock back toward its 332.32 buy point.
article.watch: Whether Cloudflare holds the 21-day line at 338.65 into its Oct. 29 report.

market_note: The S&P 500 slipped 0.2% to 7801.77 and the Nasdaq fell 0.2% to 27538.69; both still sit above their 50-day lines, by 1.6% and 4.1%. The Dow lost 0.7% to 51179.87 and trades 2.8% below its 50-day line, carrying 6 distribution days against 5 for the S&P 500 and 3 for the Nasdaq over the last 25 sessions. The desk's label stays at Uptrend under pressure. Leadership is narrow and concentrated in AI chips and networking: Astera Labs, Palo Alto Networks, Zeta Global, Arista Networks and Nvidia are all in buy range after breaking out this week, the AI chip group leads with an average RS of 87 and 92% of its members above the 50-day line, and after hours Applied Digital rose 3.7% to 24.70 from a 23.81 close.
